parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about Hayley Moore. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
Thirteen-year-old Hayley Moore has lived in five different countries. 'It's because of my mum's job,' she explains. 'So I don't go to school; I study online. My computer's in my bedroom, so that's my classroom! I have to do all the same subjects as other students, but there's no timetable. That's the best thing. I can do my classes at any time.'

Hayley studies alone, but she often goes out with friends. 'Most people my age have hobbies like dancing or sports,' says Hayley. 'I've done those things too, but I thought they were boring. So when Mum told me about the circus club, I was really excited. It takes a long time to get there, but I love it.'

Hayley's favourite activity at the club is riding the unicycle – a bicycle with only one wheel. 'You sit on a seat just above the wheel, and there's nowhere to hold on! When I started, I fell off all the time, but that's the same for everyone. You just have to keep practising – which is what I do when I don't have homework!'

Next summer, when there are no lessons, Hayley is going to go to a circus summer camp. 'It's a camp for teenagers who are interested in the circus. I'm not going to see my family for a few weeks, but that's OK. I love the unicycle, but people from a real circus are going to teach us what they do in their shows, and I can't wait!'

items.question: Hayley likes studying online because she can choose
Why did Hayley decide to try circus classes?
options: She didn't enjoy the other activities she tried.
The circus club isn't far from her home.
She didn't know many people her age.

items.question: What does Hayley say about riding the unicycle?
options: It was easier for her than for other people.
She needs to practise it more.

items.question: Hayley is excited about the circus summer camp because
options: she is going to meet other teenagers who like circuses.
she is going to learn something new.
she is going to be in a show.

parts.title: Listening Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.question: You will hear two friends talking about their plans for the weekend. What do they decide to do?
You will hear a boy asking his friend Andres about yesterday evening. What was Andres doing?
You will hear a girl leaving a message about a competition. What does the girl want to do in the competition?
You will hear two friends talking about going to a museum. How are they going to travel?
You will hear a boy talking about a concert. Why is he going to the concert?
options: His friend is going to sing.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 1. You will hear two friends talking about their plans for the weekend. What do they decide to do?

script.speaker: Girl 1
script.text: What shall we do this weekend? Are there any good films on?

script.speaker: Girl 2
script.text: I'm going to the cinema this evening – I don't want to go twice. What about that photography exhibition you mentioned that you want to see?

script.speaker: Girl 1
script.text: But you don't like photography. How about a concert?

script.speaker: Girl 2
script.text: There's nothing on that I fancy seeing. It's OK. <u>Let's go and see the photos</u>.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 2. You will hear a boy asking his friend Andres about yesterday evening. What was Andres doing?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: What were you doing when I called you yesterday, Andres? It sounded fun!

script.speaker: Andres
script.text: <u>My sister was showing me a video that her friend has posted on a website</u>. It's of him playing a computer game.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Oh, that actually sounds rather boring!

script.speaker: Andres
script.text: Not at all! It's really fun! He's so good at it. He's going to be on TV soon.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 3. You will hear a girl leaving a message about a competition. What does the girl want to do in the competition?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Hi, Marco. I'm calling about the competition. I know you want us to dance together, but I think lots of people will dance, so I want to do something different. <u>I'm fairly good at the piano now, and I've got a good song to play</u>. It's one you know. Why don't you sing it and I'll accompany you? Call me!

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 4. You will hear two friends talking about going to a museum. How are they going to travel?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: I looked online to see where the museum is. There's a train station pretty near it.

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: Oh, I forgot to say – <u>my brother's happy to drive us there</u>. It's on his way to work.

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Doesn't your brother go to work by bus?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: He's just passed his driving test, so no more buses for him!

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: Or for us! That's great. Thanks.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 5. You will hear a boy talking about a concert. Why is he going to the concert?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: I'm really sorry, but I can't go out with you tomorrow. I forgot that I'm going to a concert. The Kingpins are playing. I don't really like them but <u>they're my sister's favourite – she's mad about them</u>. Why don't you come? There are still tickets for sale. And I know your friend Emin will be there. He's always singing Kingpins songs!

parts.sampleAnswer:
Hi Sunita,
I am going to see the Beijing circus next week in Central Park. Would you like to come with me? You'll love it because you love clowns.
It starts at 3 p.m. but I think we should meet earlier. What about 2:30 outside the ticket office? You can get the number 13 bus there or you can cycle – it's not far.
Speak soon,

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about becoming an actor. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
If you have decided to be a doctor or an engineer, it's easy to get information about how to become one. It's more difficult if you want to be an actor. Nobody can say, 'First you do this, then you do that, and one day you're an actor.' But I can tell you some things that will help.

Learning to be an actor usually starts at school. Drama lessons and clubs can teach students many things, including different ways of acting and how to write their own plays. Writing helps you understand a lot about acting. But even more important is learning to work in a group with other actors.

However, school lessons and clubs are only one part of learning about being an actor. Find small theatre groups near where you live – and don't worry about being the star! It doesn't matter if you only have one word to say in a play, it will still help you to improve. You need to be on stage as much as possible, in a variety of different types of plays.

When you finish school, you should think about studying at university. Of course, it's possible to be an actor without going to university, but doing a theatre course is a good idea for some people. These courses may improve your acting, and also help you learn about a variety of subjects, such as business, history, music and dance.

items.question: What does the writer say is difficult if you want to act?
options: deciding if it's a good job for you
finding out what you need to do
telling people why you want to do it

items.question: What does the writer believe is the most useful thing to learn at school?
What advice does the writer give in the third paragraph?
options: Meet theatre stars who live near you.
Learn about all kinds of jobs in theatres.

items.question: What does the writer think about university for people who want to be actors?
options: It is the best thing to do after school.
It is good if they study lots of subjects.
It is not always important for them.

parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.question: You will hear a girl talking about the job she wants to do. What does she want to be?
You will hear Ravi talking to his dad. What are they discussing?
options: when a sports programme will finish
when Ravi should do his homework
when is the best time to have dinner

items.question: You will hear Holly talking about going to the library. Why is she going there?
You will hear Rosie telling her mum about an exhibition. What was wrong with the exhibition?
options: Rosie couldn't see the whole exhibition.

items.question: You will hear a boy talking to his mum about his lunch. What is he going to make for lunch?

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 1. You will hear a girl talking about the job she wants to do. What does she want to be?

script.speaker: Girl
script.text: At school, I enjoy my art lessons, especially photography. My art teacher gave me some tips about taking great pictures on a trip to Kripps Lake. I also enjoy writing stories and finding out about people's lives. So <u>I'd really like to put all those things together, and get a job on a newspaper or a magazine</u>. But I don't think that'll be easy!

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 2. You will hear Ravi talking to his dad. What are they discussing?

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: Haven't you got to do some maths exercises before dinner, Ravi? It's going to be ready in an hour.

script.speaker: Ravi
script.text: I'll do them later, Dad – I want to watch a basketball game.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: <u>You must do them before you watch TV.</u>

script.speaker: Ravi
script.text: OK. I'll do them now. I'll watch the game online after dinner.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 3. You will hear Holly talking about going to the library. Why is she going there?

script.speaker: Holly
script.text: After my last lesson, I'm going to the school library. I need a book for my history research and they don't have it on the shelves – I checked online today. So <u>I'm going to ask Mrs Stewart at the library to get it for me</u>. She's really nice. I did this before, and the book arrived in about three days. I took it back yesterday.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 4. You will hear Rosie telling her mum about an exhibition. What was wrong with the exhibition?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: So why didn't you enjoy the exhibition, Rosie?

script.speaker: Rosie
script.text: Well, Mum, there were lots of interesting paintings. <u>I just wasn't sure what most of them were, or what they meant.</u>

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Oh. There are usually signs next to the pictures which tell you about them.

script.speaker: Rosie
script.text: Not for this exhibition. There was just one poster, about the painter's life.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: 5. You will hear a boy talking to his mum about lunch. What is he going to make for lunch?

script.speaker: Boy
script.text: I'm going to make lunch for us, Mum. There are lots of vegetables in the fridge – <u>I'll cut them into little pieces and heat them in a pan with some water and some tomatoes</u>, and lots of pepper and salt … and perhaps a bit of pasta. Then we'll have a nice hot bowl of it with some bread. OK?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Sounds lovely!
